data.title: Bitcoin Bounces as Market Optimism Returns After Holiday
data.description: Bitcoin bounced on Friday as traders prepared for a bumper return to US trading after the US holiday. According to Bloomberg, technology stocks were set to rally when markets opened.

data.title: Velio Bets on Taiwan's AI Supply Chain for Its Perpetual DEX
data.description: Velio is targeting assets not yet covered by Hyperliquid and has listed perpetual contracts tied to U.S.-listed AI-related assets, including Nvidia, TSMC ADR, and QQQ, as well as gold. According to PANews, Taiwanese stocks are undergoing internal testing and are expected to launch in December, with the first batch including MediaTek, TSMC, ASE Technology, and UMC.

data.title: Stretch's Effective Yield Is 12.24% as It Targets Bitcoin-Based Three-Month Digital Credit Benchmark
data.description: Stretch (STRC) had an effective yield of 12.24% on November 25, while the quoted discount rate for the U.S. 13-week Treasury bill (IRX) was 4.16%. According to Odaily, Michael Saylor said in a post on X that Stretch aims to become the three-month benchmark for bitcoin-based digital credit.

data.title: Bittensor Raises Subnet Limit to 160; @const_reborn Sees Potential for 512 or More
data.description: Bittensor has raised its subnet limit to 160, and @const_reborn said it could eventually reach 512 or more. According to Odaily, the OpenTensor Foundation said on X that the increase lowers registration costs and gives smaller teams more time to build and demonstrate their capabilities, as discussed by Const in the latest episode of Novelty Search. Const, @markjeffrey and @mogmachine also discussed using Gamma to bring Bittensor’s AI services to users outside the network and plans for permissionless lending to increase subnet liquidity.

data.title: Conferences Are Becoming Newsrooms as Coverage Extends Beyond Events
data.description: Conferences are increasingly functioning as newsrooms, with their value extending beyond attendance to the coverage and content they generate. BeInCrypto’s TOKEN2049 Singapore coverage reached readers after the event ended, according to BeInCrypto, with 49% of article readership coming afterward and 46% reading in a language other than English. Over two days in October 2026, its NewsDesk recorded 24 interviews that became 56 videos, clips and newsletter features; coverage totaled 117 pieces across 26 language editions and other channels, with potential reach exceeding 8.8 million. The article announcing The State of AI Agent Payments 2026 received 83% of its views after the event. More broadly, 54% of commercial publishers surveyed by the Reuters Institute in 2026 identified online and in-person events as an important revenue stream. The article also points to AI discovery as a reason event coverage can have a longer life: Muck Rack found earned media accounted for about 84% of links cited by AI assistants. Organizers and publishers still face cost pressures and difficulty measuring return on investment.

data.title: LlamaRisk Proposes Lower Aave V3 Supply and Borrowing Caps for WBTC and LINK, Plus USDC Rate Model Changes
data.description: LlamaRisk proposed lowering supply and borrowing caps for several assets on Aave V3 and changing the USDC interest-rate model. According to Foresight News, the Aave risk service provider based its recommendations on user behavior, on-chain liquidity and position health. In the Core market, it proposed reducing WBTC’s supply cap from 41,000 to 39,000 tokens and LINK’s from 8 million to 7.6 million tokens, while lowering LINK’s borrowing cap from 500,000 to 300,000 tokens. It also recommended reducing USDC’s optimal usage ratio from 91% to 90%. In the Mantle market, LlamaRisk proposed cutting USDe’s supply cap from 25 million to 10 million tokens and its borrowing cap from 10 million to 5 million tokens. At USDC’s current utilization rate of 79.3%, the adjustment would increase its floating annual borrowing rate from 4.22% to 4.26%. The changes would be implemented through the Risk Steward process.

data.title: AI | JPMorgan’s Lecubarri Sees Midcap Value After Second-Biggest-Ever Underperformance
data.description: Small- and mid-cap stocks have recorded the second-biggest underperformance in the asset class’s history, JPMorgan Research’s global head of small- and mid-cap strategy Eduardo Lecubarri said on Bloomberg’s “The Opening Trade,” according to Bloomberg. He said 73% of AI-related stocks are not included in any AI-traded ETF and that smaller companies offer unusually strong value.

data.title: UK FCA Proposes DeFi Access Limits for Regulated Exchanges and Platform Rules for Tokenized Stocks
data.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is proposing rules that would require DeFi service providers to obtain authorization and prohibit regulated exchanges from directing retail customers to decentralized markets. According to Odaily, trading in tokenized stocks would also have to take place on regulated platforms; the proposals have not yet taken effect.

data.title: Joachim Nagel: ECB Likely Needs Another Rate Hike in December
data.description: Stubborn inflation means the European Central Bank will probably need to raise interest rates again next month, Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Bank Indonesia Prioritizes Stability and Inflation Control in 2027
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Bank Indonesia will focus on stability next year and pursue monetary policy to keep inflation within its target range while facing sustained pressure on the rupiah.

data.title: Chainflip Identifies Vault Attack Entry Point, Says Protocol Won’t Restart Before Security Review
data.description:
Chainflip said its second report on attacks against its Bitcoin and Ethereum vaults identified the attack method, completed a full accounting of losses and covered discussions with all major active liquidity providers. According to Odaily, those providers said they would resume supplying liquidity once the security review and remediation meet requirements and a recapitalization plan is implemented.

The investigation identified validator software for peer-to-peer communications based on ZeroMQ (libzmq) as the attack entry point. It found no evidence linking the attack to flaws in the vault smart contracts, threshold-signature scheme or State Chain logic. Chainflip said the stolen Bitcoin has not moved, while the Ethereum funds deposited into Tornado Cash may also remain unmoved.

data.title: Norse Atlantic Files for Bankruptcy in Europe After Failing to Secure Funding
data.description: According to CNBC, Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy in Europe Friday after failing to secure funding, as soaring fuel costs strained the airline’s operations throughout the year. Its parent company, Norse Atlantic ASA, said the Norwegian carrier no longer had a basis to continue operating and had been unable to secure enough funding to meet its short-term liquidity needs.

data.title: US Goods-Trade Gap Expands for Fourth Consecutive Month
data.description: The US merchandise-trade deficit widened for a fourth straight month in October as imports of capital goods continued to grow, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Binance Market Update | Asia Rallies as KOSPI Jumps 4.34% and Hang Seng Tech 6.45%, Bitcoin Reclaims $61K on Short Squeeze as Stocks Rebound
data.description: Asian stocks surged Friday, with the Hang Seng Tech Index up 6.45%, the KOSPI up 4.34% and ChiNext up more than 7%, after China's State Council pledged more market support. US futures also rose, with Nasdaq futures up about 2.4% premarket and SanDisk up 11%. Bitcoin rose 1.8% to about $61,600, though short liquidations (71% of the total) drove much of the move and it still lags stocks. The S&P 500 entered a correction on November 20, but Deutsche Bank says none of the usual bear market triggers is present yet. Short-term bitcoin holders sit on an average 15% loss, a zone that has historically coincided with bottoms.S&P 500 Enters Correction; Bear Markets and Recessions Don't Always FollowThe S&P 500 entered a correction on November 20, its first since April 2025, falling 3.7% to 6,910.39, which is 11.6% below its October 6 closing high of 7,818.93. Eight of the 13 S&P 500 bear markets overlapped with recessions, while five did not. Deutsche Bank's Henry Allen said bear markets since 1962 coincided with at least one of three conditions: a recession, data deterioration that raised recession fears, or a cycle of Fed hikes. He said none is present so far. The November flash composite PMI was 54.6, indicating expansion, and markets are pricing fewer Fed hikes through September 2027 than on October 6.Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Sit on 15% Average Loss as STH MVRV Falls to 0.85, Near July LowShort-term holder MVRV fell to 0.85, almost matching its July low of 0.81 (July 1), per CryptoQuant's Darkfost. It peaked at 1.18 on September 22. A reading below 1 means holders are at an average loss. Darkfost puts the short-term holder cost basis at $71,600, implying about a 15% unrealized loss. He said such levels "have historically coincided with bottom formation" and can offer opportunities for long-term investors.Short Liquidations Hit 71% as Crypto Trails a 4% Weekly Stock Rally; Monero Falls 13% on DelistingsBitcoin rose 1.8% to about $61,600 as US markets reopened for a half-day session, lagging Nasdaq 100 futures (+2.6%). It is up 0.6% this week; holding through Sunday's close would end seven straight weekly losses, the second-longest streak on record. It is still down about 20% in November. The S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Dow are each up about 4% on the week. Liquidations fell 61% to $242M, 71% of them shorts (77% of the $84.7M in bitcoin liquidations), and bitcoin open interest barely changed, which points to short covering. About $7B of bitcoin options expired at 08:00 UTC. Four of the six most traded options were calls; the busiest single contract was the December 25 $50,000 put. Ether options remain defensive, with all six busiest contracts puts. XMR fell 13% after two other exchanges said they will delist it on November 30, citing EU rules on privacy coins; ZEC rose 11%. The CoinDesk 80 rose 1.9%, FET 5.9%, TAO 2.4%. Fear and Greed stood at 11, extreme fear, and the Altcoin Season Index at 63.Hang Seng Tech Jumps 6.45% and KOSPI 4.34% as Chip and AI Stocks Lead Asian RallyThe Hang Seng rose 2.11%, KOSDAQ 8.13%, ChiNext more than 7% and the Nikkei 2.11% to 58,711.11. Zhipu rose 18.57%, MiniMax 17.19% and SMIC more than 16%. The KOSPI closed up 204.47 points at 4,915.68, with foreign investors buying a net ₩1.13T, the most since September 7; SK Hynix rose 6.42% and Samsung 4.55%. Korea's National Pension Service lost about ₩202T in Q3, down 10.8% to ₩1,664T. In China, more than 4,900 stocks rose after the State Council pledged to improve market stabilization, encourage dividends and buybacks, and provide liquidity. Unitree gained as much as 13.66%.SanDisk Jumps 11% and Nvidia 4% Premarket as Memory and Optical Stocks Lead an AI ReboundPremarket (thin volume, may not hold): Nasdaq futures +2.40%, S&P 500 futures +1.79%, Dow futures +1.41%. SanDisk +11.14%, Seagate +7.20%, Western Digital +7.03%, Micron +6.63%, Marvell +7.69%, Nvidia +3.88%. Optical: AXT +10.98%, Applied Optoelectronics +9.26%, Coherent +8.73%, Lumentum +8.38%. Nebius +9.48%, CoreWeave nearly +8%, Anthropic +4.20%. Crypto-linked stocks rose about 5% to 6%. China semiconductor ETFs jumped up to 18%, and the four largest Chinese banks signed more than 600B yuan of buyback loans with listed companies.
